paragraphs: The S65 AMG represents the pinnacle of the S-Class range - a V12-powered flagship that sits above even the V8 S63 AMG. Across its two generations (W221, 2008-2013, and W222, 2013-2020), the S65 AMG has used a single engine: the M275, a 6.0-litre twin-turbo V12. It's a complex and highly specialised unit, and rebuilding it requires the same level of care and expertise as the car's original assembly. The S65 AMG was discontinued after the W222 generation - the V12 role in the current W223 range moved to the Maybach S680 instead. The S65 AMG is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S65 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the S65 AMG from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the S65 AMG uses a specialised V12 that was only fitted to the flagship S-Class and a handful of other AMG models, engine compatibility is critical. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
